unclaimed_findings: if-no-files-found: warn makes the retention guarantee unenforced at runtime. Nothing in CI refuses a job that produced no observation records. If verify.py crashes before line 208, if --observe is silently dropped by a future argparse change, or if the matrix's fail-fast cancels a leg before verify runs, the artifact is simply absent and the retention step is green with a warning. Sibling steps in the same three jobs use if-no-files-found: error for their subject receipts, so this is a deliberate asymmetry in the permissive direction. It is also the opposite choice from scripts/sovland/isolation.py, which the workflow header names as the model: isolation.py's fallback on an unreadable observation file makes the gate stricter, explicitly 'so a problem in this module makes the gate stricter rather than more permissive'.

Nothing anywhere reads the retained artifacts. No check, script, or report consumes a CI observations artifact; scripts/sovland/isolation.py reads its own locally produced file. Retention with no consumer plus if-no-files-found: warn means an empty, truncated, or absent artifact would never be noticed by anything.

No test exercises the --observe CLI end to end. scripts/tests/test_verify_observations.py calls verify.observe(...) as a function; no test calls main(['--observe', path]) and asserts the file exists and parses. The workflows' whole guarantee depends on that flag surface, and the only thing checking it is the workflow text.

A legal form is over-refused: an observe path templated from the matrix, e.g. --observe "$RUNNER_TEMP/${{ matrix.python-version }}-observations.json", fails OBSERVE_TARGET's [\w.-]+ and is reported as 'does not pass --observe'. Conservative rather than dangerous, but it forecloses a form a future author would reasonably reach for.

hygiene-repair.yml is declared INTEGRATION in contracts/repository-ci-evidence.json but has no sov_ci_subject.py binding step, so hygiene-observations-${{ github.sha }} is the first identity assertion that workflow makes and it supplies one of the five elements INTEGRATION required_identity names. Pre-existing, not introduced here, but the new artifact name is what surfaces it.

The observations artifact and its sibling subject receipt are keyed differently in verify.yml's repository job: repository-observations-<merge sha> against integration-ci-subject-<base>-<head>. They are pairable only because artifacts are scoped to one run. No collision is possible within a run: upload-artifact@v4 rejects duplicate names, and all four names differ by prefix and by python-version suffix.

'Unconditionally' is true at the step level and not at the run level. verify.yml's candidate job is gated `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'`, and fail-fast: true can cancel the second matrix leg before its verify step runs. Both are pre-existing job-level facts, not changes made here.

No secret or host path exposure: the 52 records carry only repository-relative addresses, sha256 digests, exit codes, timings, and observer prose. Checked the serialized payload for /home/ and for drive-letter paths; neither appears.
residuals: The refusal in claim 8 is the material one. The claim's second half - 'a new test class refuses any future verify step that does not' - is not reproduced. Seven legal YAML or filesystem forms bypass it, one of them (`run: >-`) already the house idiom in the same files. The guard is a regex over raw text where a yaml.safe_load over the same bytes would see every form; the repository pins standard library only, so the tradeoff is real, but the current predicate can be strengthened without a parser: match the verify invocation across folded and literal scalars, glob *.yaml as well as *.yml, and scope the upload search to the same job.
The check reads the artifact rather than a report about it, which is the right side of the AGENTS.md line: it grades the bytes GitHub will execute. Its defect is reach, not subject.

This observation was taken against a tree byte-identical to 714337a and confirmed stable across two full verify runs. It says nothing about b1448ee, about the composition of 714337a with current main, or about how CI behaves on a hosted runner; every command here ran locally.

overall_verdict: PARTIALLY REPRODUCED, WITH DISSENT. The retention half of the claim holds under independent reading: four verify invocations, four --observe flags, four matching if: always() uploads, a schema-valid 52-record file, and records that provably survive a failing run. The refusal half does not hold. The three declared defeating cases fire, but the guard they defend is defeatable by seven legal forms, including the folded `run: >-` scalar these same workflows already use for their other multi-word commands. Combined with if-no-files-found: warn and the absence of any consumer for the artifacts, the guarantee is presently static-text-only: nothing at any layer refuses a CI run that produced no observation records. That goes back to the builder for repair inside this concern.
